text: Welcome, I am Dr. Agent. You mention a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation; to help me understand your condition, are you experiencing severe headaches, neck stiffness, or seizures?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS) secondary to haloperidol use. The combination of fever, altered mentation, and a history of tics treated with haloperidol is highly suggestive of NMS, even in the absence of severe headache or neck stiffness.
